convoLines.text: "Can we talk?" Brayden sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"...I should say, I trade in what I know. My knowledge for yours. Or food, if you're short on secrets."
"Huh. Let me think about that." Nobody touches this group. Not while I'm standing.
"I sleep lighter than I used to. Someone has to hear things first."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on wanting to protect the group. Anyway."
"One day at a time, that's the plan. What did you want to ask?"
"I saw the woman in her 30s, with a nervous tic go down. I did what I could. It wasn't enough, and I carry that now."
You show them Lamb's Quarters — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"I should go before I say something sincere."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About this wound — I still haven't found anyone. Any chance?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Get to their side of the Haven door and stand next to them — then you can help.
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"Pedunculate Oak Acorn. Remember the leaf, the stem, the smell — that's the whole of it."
"This one is Camu-camu. Look at the leaf, feel the stem, breathe it in. It'll stick."
Gerald looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
They let the words sit there, unanswered.
"Right. I get it." A beat — and then the subject is closed. For today, anyway.
"Still on that wound care."
"Right. Done. Don't look so relieved."
"No — you're right, it's a lot. Forget it."
"Same time tomorrow, maybe."
"You look handy. What did you do with your hands, before?"
"I'm not sure, but Useful. Everything useful matters now. I mean that as a compliment."
"These hands? Night security guard hands. Clipboards, mostly. Now they hold wire and wood, and they learn fast. Hands are honest that way."
"Still on what you did with your hands."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Marcus owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Mia grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
